audit_findings.title: Noncash finance-lease capex may escape the maintenance-capex deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; FY2026 finance-lease additions were $441.1 million, amortization was $243.6 million, and principal payments were $241.6 million
audit_findings.mechanism: If finance-lease depreciation is added back in OE without an offsetting maintenance replacement charge, anchor OE and every scenario are overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: Depreciation of property, plant and equipment, including finance lease assets, is calculated primarily using the straight-line method over the estimated useful lives of the assets, which range from two to 39 years , and is included primarily in operating expenses on the consolidated statements of operations.
audit_findings.explanation: No omission is demonstrated because the detailed OE bridge is absent. The exposure is nevertheless material: finance-lease amortization equals 37.3% of the $653.6 million anchor, while new finance-lease assets equal 67.5%. Only the maintenance portion should be charged, and principal must not also be deducted if that would double count the same asset renewal.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct the FY2026 OE bridge asset by asset, identify finance-lease depreciation added back, classify the maintenance portion of the $441.1 million additions, and rerun all scenarios with one—and only one—economic replacement charge.

audit_findings.title: Growth may require material working-capital reinvestment not visible in the valuation
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified forecast omission; receivables plus inventory less trade payables increased $138.5 million to $3,693.9 million in FY2026, equal to 21.2% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Incremental receivables and inventory, net of supplier financing, reduce distributable OE required to support the 3% and 6% growth scenarios through the RONTA reinvestment calculation.
audit_findings.evidence: Our borrowing levels are subject to seasonal fluctuations, as well as procurement and acquisition activities.
audit_findings.explanation: The stated 10% RONTA suggests some reinvestment is modeled, so an error is not demonstrated. However, the record does not show that working capital is included in the operating asset base. The filed balance-sheet movement is large relative to OE, and the growth scenarios add $1,408 million and $3,060 million of equity value over the zero-growth case, making omission reasonably capable of materially overstating those scenarios.
audit_findings.action: Provide the RONTA denominator and forecast reinvestment schedule, reconcile it to receivables, inventory, payables and other operating assets, separate acquisition and seasonal movements, and rerun base and bull cases if working capital was excluded.

audit_findings.title: Deferred acquisition consideration is an omitted claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $23.4 million face amount; at most $0.14 per diluted share before present-value discounting, or 0.25% of the $9,276 million base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any amount not already recognized in OE or another bridge item should be deducted as an acquisition-related claim against common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: As of June 27, 2026 , the deferred consideration payable to the seller was $ 23.4 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The omitted-claim possibility is unresolved, but its filed face amount supplies a conservative ceiling. Deducting the entire $23.4 million would reduce base value from $57.17 to approximately $57.03 per share and would not materially alter the valuation conclusion or the gap to the $98.63 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm where the seller payable is recorded and whether related expense is already captured; if absent from both OE and the bridge, deduct its present value without changing operating inputs.

audit_findings.title: Vendor-rebate estimates could inflate the latest OE anchor
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; $121.6 million of vendor rebates and promotional incentives was netted against inventory at FY2026 year-end
audit_findings.mechanism: An excessive rebate accrual understates COGS, overstates FY2026 earnings and OE, and is propagated through the sole latest-actual anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Auditing the volume based vendor rebates involved significant audit effort to evaluate whether vendor consideration is recorded in accordance with the terms of the vendor agreements.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing establishes estimation dependence and identifies vendor rebates as a significant profit source, but it does not demonstrate an erroneous accrual or quantify total FY2026 rebate income at risk. The auditor tested agreements, confirmations, collections and estimate adjustments, yet the valuation record lacks the detailed reconciliation needed to determine whether the anchor contains a material overestimate.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the FY2026 rebate roll-forward by program, executed terms, purchasing-volume calculations, subsequent cash receipts and post-year-end true-ups; adjust the anchor and rerun only for supported misestimates.

audit_findings.title: The null perimeter and latest-actual anchor may mishandle US Foods clean-team costs
audit_findings.magnitude: $20.2 million FY2026 expense; transaction-perimeter effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: If the process remained live, a null standalone perimeter may be invalid; if it had ended and the cost is nonrecurring, retaining the expense depresses normalized OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Additionally, for the fiscal year ended June 27, 2026, Other adjustments includes $20.2 million of legal and professional fees incurred in connection with shareholder activism and the clean team agreement with US Foods Holding Corp.
audit_findings.explanation: The $20.2 million charge equals 3.1% of the $653.6 million anchor before tax, but the record does not show its treatment in OE or establish the US Foods process status on September 5, 2026. The expense issue points toward understated value, while an active transaction could change the valuation perimeter in an unquantified direction.
audit_findings.action: Establish the process status as of the valuation date from definitive company disclosures, reconcile the $20.2 million to the OE bridge, and rerun either a supported standalone normalization or the appropriate transaction/perimeter case.

audit_findings.title: Future interest cost may diverge from the FY2026 equity-OE burden
audit_findings.magnitude: $18.2 million annual pre-tax interest change per 100-basis-point SOFR move on approximately $1.8 billion of variable-rate debt; $2,971.0 million matures in fiscal 2030
audit_findings.mechanism: Because interest remains in equity-level OE, changes in floating rates and refinancing costs alter forecast OE directly without requiring a separate debt-principal deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: A hypothetical 100 bps increase in SOFR on our variable-rate debt would lead to an increase of approximately $18.2 million in annual interest expense.
audit_findings.explanation: The FY2026 interest burden is already reflected in the anchor; the finding concerns future rates and refinancing terms rather than a demonstrated current error. Rates could raise or lower value, and the 2030 maturity falls within the explicit forecast horizon, so the exposure should be monitored and scenario-tested as terms become observable.
audit_findings.action: Update projected OE for actual SOFR, hedge coverage and refinancing terms; rerun rate sensitivities around the $18.2 million-per-100-basis-point exposure and the fiscal-2030 maturity without deducting principal separately.
